name: Tryptophan to Indole-3-Acetic Acid (IAA) Network
notes: Two prokaryotic biosynthetic routes from tryptophan to indole-3-acetic acid (IAA/auxin). IAA production is widespread in bacteria and affects plant-microbe interactions. Additional plant-specific pathways exist (tryptamine pathway, nitrile pathways via CYP450 enzymes) but are excluded from this potato. Converted from GATOR v1 'Tryptophan to IAA' pathways I and III.

genes.name: tryptophan 2-monooxygenase
genes.notes: Converts tryptophan → indole-3-acetamide. Key gene in IAM pathway (bacteria).

genes.name: amidase
genes.notes: Converts indole-3-acetamide → IAA. Found in paths I and V.

genes.name: indoleacetamide hydrolase
genes.notes: Alternative to amiE for indole-3-acetamide → IAA conversion.

genes.name: aldehyde dehydrogenase (NAD+)
genes.notes: Converts indole-3-acetaldehyde → IAA. Broad substrate specificity, found in bacteria.

genes.name: L-amino-acid oxidase
genes.notes: Converts tryptophan → indolepyruvate. Broad substrate specificity.

genes.name: aromatic amino acid aminotransferase I / 2-aminoadipate transaminase
genes.notes: Broad specificity aminotransferase, can convert tryptophan → indolepyruvate.

genes.name: indolepyruvate decarboxylase
genes.notes: Converts indolepyruvate → indole-3-acetaldehyde. Key marker for IPA pathway.

iaam_pathway.name: IAM Pathway (iaaM pathway)
iaam_pathway.notes: Bacterial pathway. Two-step: tryptophan → indole-3-acetamide → IAA. Common in Agrobacterium, Pseudomonas.

scoring.notes: iaaM is diagnostic marker. Either amiE or iaaH required for second step.

indolepyruvate_pathway.name: Indolepyruvate Pathway (IPA pathway)
indolepyruvate_pathway.notes: Bacterial three-step pathway via indolepyruvate. ipdC is diagnostic marker. Common in plant-associated bacteria.

scoring.notes: ipdC is diagnostic marker for bacterial IPA pathway. Requires at least one aminotransferase (IL4I1, Tam1, or ARO8) plus ipdC and ALDH.
